subject: Insurance
title: September 11: The Biggest Insured Loss
description: A quick win: understand September 11: The Biggest Insured Loss.

hook.text: The 9/11 attacks caused $45 billion in insured losses—the largest single insurance event in history at the time.

buildup.text: Property, life, liability, workers' comp, and aviation claims all hit simultaneously.

discovery.text: Larry Silverstein had insured the World Trade Center for $3.55 billion just weeks before the attack.

twist.text: After 9/11, insurers excluded terrorism from standard policies.

climax.text: 9/11 proved terrorism risk was real and massive. Insurance alone couldn't cover it. Only government partnership worked.

punchline.text: $45 billion in losses. 9/11 made terrorism a government-backed insurance risk.

quiz.question: What was created after 9/11 to cover terrorism risk?
